proof_summary: The cases $9$ and $27$ are obtained by direct finite minimization, while for $81$ the congruence $10^i\equiv1+9i\pmod{81}$ applied to a number and its reversal forces any smaller common candidate to have digit sum $81$, hence nine digits all equal to $9$. For every larger exponent, concatenating $3^{n-5}$ copies of the palindromic block $68899199886$ gives a palindrome divisible by $3^n$—using the block’s factor $3^5$ and a geometric-sum induction—and its digit-length bound makes it strictly smaller than the all-nines number.
